dungeon.note: Slot eligibility only; stage-next-enemy also requires strict native Ready. Appended staircase is outside definition room bounds.

materialReview.result: Configured mireglass palette was bound through the private renderer material and native emission was disabled as required by the profile.

selectedPNGs.observation: Complete authored body, head, limbs, tail and eye ornaments render together in the native combat camera.
A later idle frame retains the same coherent silhouette with no detached authored piece visible.
Native attack begins with the articulated body leaning toward the hero; head, torso, arms and tail remain joined.
Attack follow-through remains a readable crouched marsh-dragon silhouette despite native effect light.
Attack recovery returns the intact model to its standing silhouette while the hero HP indicator records native retaliation.
The actual ordinary player hit begins; the model is visible through native hit effects and retains its connected form.
Mid-hit pose visibly stretches the native skeleton without a lost authored renderer or separate detached mesh.
Hit recovery visibly restores the full bound model before later enemy action.
The explicit fixture death begins on the native death clip with the bound model still visible.
Native death effect clears the model into its designed disappearance; this frame is effect-heavy and is not a finished-art verdict.
Later death sampling shows the enemy cleared before the native loot UI; no renderer resurrection is visible.

limits: This review covers the exact acidBlobB/enAcidMonster source pair only; AcidBlob A or resource-prefab rows require their own trials.
Native combat effects and the foreground hero partly obscure close surface detail.
The explicit KillSingle transition is not ordinary lethal-damage acceptance.
The native death effect clears the enemy quickly, so this is a transition/cleanup review rather than a settled corpse or ragdoll review.
Culling envelope, portrait, long-session resource lifetime, other ability variants and final art-direction approval remain separate work.
